answer: The tide turns slow outside the harbour mouth, and the pilot reads the water by the marks on the quay. Proof of harbour pilot via tide chart log — a ship the pilot guides only after 13 ships run true, each ship charted by the pilot himself. The falcon holds the shipping list safe against the damp. The mirror maps the sandbank that shifts with every storm. The relic rings the bell that warns the boats home. A forger must guide 13 ships, chart 13 ships and prove 13 ships true, five weeks on the water for a passage that still runs aground at low tide.
